meta.title: MIT Entrance (TU) syllabus, parsed for AI question generation
meta.source: MIT_Entrance_Scope_Guide.md (canonical human-readable guide: strategy, recall webs, and generation rules)
how_to_use: Pick subject by exam_marks, then unit by share_in_subject_pct, then topic by share_in_unit_pct. global_weight_pct = probability a random exam-style question should come from that topic (sums to ~100 over all topics).

importance is 1-10 (10 = must know cold, 1 = skip). level L0-L3 is the guide's own priority: L0 core, L1 standard, L2 exact number/syntax, L3 advanced/low value. Never generate for skip:true topics unless asked for stretch practice.
Each topic is one distinct generation unit with its own id: assign topic ids to question batches, so duplicates are avoided by construction (one question family per topic id, vary slot values).
For app concept tracking, set a question's topic_id to one exact topic id and keep its subject and unit aligned; questions without an exact mapping remain usable but do not count as topic evidence.
type: recall = single fact; pair = A!=B sibling question (use confusable_with as distractor source); calc/trace = one small hand step.
Exam mix: 60-70% recall, 20-30% pair, ~10% calc/trace. Level mix: L0 50, L1 30, L2 15, L3 5.

app_tracking.mapping_rule: Exact topic ID only; do not infer concept mastery from unit or question-text similarity.
app_tracking.evidence_rule: Topic progress is derived from existing answer history and requires confident correct attempts on separate days for solid status.

generation_rules.depth_ceiling: one fact or one small step; no derivations, long programs, multi-step proofs
generation_rules.scope: only topics in this file; if unsure, exclude
generation_rules.distractors: from misconceptions: sibling concept, classic calc slip, or one wrong word
generation_rules.options: 4 options within ~20% length; key balanced a-d; All-of-above rare (~6 in 80)
generation_rules.subject_blocks: each subject in one unbroken run per set
